environment.description: AWS Lambda (Node.js 18.x) deployed in a hardened account. The KMS key is backed by a CloudHSM cluster (CUSTOM_KEY_STORE with cloudhsm-hsm backing). The key policy uses a condition that restricts kms:Sign operations to requests where the 'kms:EncryptionContext:operation' context key equals 'login-session-issuance'. The /api/elevate-role handler calls kms.sign() without passing any EncryptionContext, so the signToken() call within that handler will be DENIED by KMS key policy. Additionally, the Lambda execution role has a permissions boundary (arn:aws:iam::ACCOUNT:policy/HSMSigningBoundary) that includes a Deny statement for kms:Sign unless aws:RequestTag/signing-purpose equals 'initial-auth'. The /api/internal/bootstrap path is mapped to a separate Lambda integration that is only invocable from a VPC endpoint (vpce-0a1b2c3d4e) with a resource policy restricting source VPC. The net effect: the elevate-role endpoint can verify existing signatures (kms:Verify is unrestricted) but CANNOT produce new signed admin tokens because the Sign call lacks the required encryption context and request tags, and the HSM-backed key will reject the operation at the hardware level.

config.api_gateway_bootstrap: separate integration, resource policy: aws:SourceVpce = vpce-0a1b2c3d4e
config.network: Lambda in private subnet, API Gateway with mutual TLS
